normal_consistency — 3D metrics op

• Data kinds: points × normals → measurement

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.normal_consistency(points_a, normals_a, points_b, normals_b) (to call the implementation directly, import metrics3d; metrics3d.normal_consistency(points_a, normals_a, points_b, normals_b); from the registry, ops3d.get("normal_consistency"))

Usage

Normal agreement over nearest-neighbour correspondences = mean|cos(na, nb)| (orientation ignored). → [0,1]. 1 = perfect agreement.

Raises ValueError: if a point cloud is empty or not (N,3), or the normals are not 1-to-1 with the points.

Computation: for each point of points_a, take the nearest neighbour in points_b (cKDTree, k=1), normalise that point's normal nb and its own normal na to unit length (divide by norm + 1e-12) and average |na · nb|. Since the absolute value is taken, a mismatch in normal orientation (front/back) is ignored. Asymmetric (only the one direction a → b. If the reverse is needed, swap the arguments and call again).

Arguments: points_a (N, 3), normals_a (N, 3), points_b (M, 3), normals_b (M, 3). It checks that all 4 are non-empty (*, 3) and that the row count of the normals matches the row count of the corresponding point cloud (violations raise ValueError). A zero normal is divided by 1e-12 and contributes almost 0 (not an error).

Returns: Python float, [0, 1]. 1 = normals parallel in all correspondences. For random normal pairs the expected value in 3-D is about 0.5 (the mean of the absolute cos).

Note: it does not look at positional closeness (even a distant nearest neighbour only has its normal compared). To evaluate together with position, combine it with chamfer_distance / fscore. For a cloud without normals, create them with estimate_point_normals (local PCA) before passing it in.
